name: btc_regime_classifier_evaluation_framework
status: PRE-REGISTERED — evaluation FRAMEWORK. Individual runs instantiate it and inherit its gates verbatim.

why_this_exists.the_error_being_corrected: G3/G3b/G4 all made TRADED RETURN the headline gate for a regime classifier. That evaluated a description-defined object with an entry-model criterion. The same arc had already established that regime labels are description-defined and therefore cannot be scored by PnL.
why_this_exists.the_measurement_that_proves_it: G3b OOS: the learned detector (agree 61.8, 47-bar runs, 357 switches, traded -55.66%) versus the no-learning czz1.2 (agree 60.5, 46-bar runs, 315 switches, traded +128.39%). At MATCHED persistence and MATCHED turnover, 1.3pp more label agreement came with 184 percentage points LESS traded return. Agreement and PnL are close to unrelated here, in both directions.
why_this_exists.the_mechanism: agreement weights every bar equally; PnL weights bars by |return|. A price-based rule concentrates its errors on small moves by construction; a learned probability model carries no such alignment and lands errors on large moves.
why_this_exists.consequence: PnL is removed from regime-classifier scoring entirely. It is neither a gate nor a tiebreak nor a reported headline.

scope.evaluates: a CAUSAL regime classifier against a regime LABEL, on descriptive grounds only
scope.does_not_evaluate: whether the regime is tradeable, what it should be sized at, or whether any downstream consumer benefits. Those are separate contracts with their own gates.
scope.no_pnl_anywhere: no traded return, no MDD, no sizing, no cost model appears in any gate or headline of this framework.

axis_1_descriptive_validity.question: Do the states differ in measurable statistical properties, and does the difference PERSIST out of sample?

split_into_two_because_they_fail_differe.1a_label_validity: run the battery on the LABEL itself. If the label's own states are not distinguishable, no classifier can fix that and axes 2-3 would be measuring fidelity to a meaningless target. 1a is therefore a PRECONDITION, checked before any classifier is trained.
split_into_two_because_they_fail_differe.1b_detector_preservation: run the same battery on the CLASSIFIER's states. A detector can have high bar agreement yet destroy the separation — e.g. by lagging enough that it assigns the calm tail of a move to the state that is supposed to be volatile. That failure is invisible to agreement and is exactly what the 2026-08-08 czz4 lag-artifact test found.

properties_measured_none_of_which_are_re: realized volatility (per-state variance of log returns)
return autocorrelation at lags 1,6,12 (trend vs mean-reverting character)
jump intensity (share of bars beyond 3x trailing sigma) and excess kurtosis
trade intensity / volume z (activity regime, independent of direction)

statistics.per_property: two-sample test between the states (Brown-Forsythe for scale, Welch t for location, permutation for the rest) reported with an EFFECT SIZE (Cohen's d or variance ratio), never a p-value alone
statistics.null: PERMUTE THE LABELLING, not the blocks — reassign the same multiset of state labels to blocks at random (circular shift preserves run structure and occupancy, destroys alignment), R>=200. The observed effect must exceed the null's 95th percentile.
statistics.window_discipline: every effect is reported SEPARATELY for train, VAL and OOS and never pooled. A pooled number hid a 67x reversal on 2026-08-08 (variance ratio 0.097 on VAL vs 6.49 on OOS, pooled to 0.881).
statistics.sign_persistence: the effect's SIGN must be identical across train, VAL and OOS. A property whose sign flips between windows is not a regime property.

axis_1_descriptive_validity.gate: at least one property must (i) exceed the permutation null's 95th percentile on OOS, (ii) keep its sign across all three windows, and (iii) show a non-trivial effect size. Properties that pass are named in the verdict; a classifier passing on volume alone is not the same claim as one passing on volatility.

axis_2_turning_point_timing.question: Does the classifier find the label's turning points, how late, and how many does it invent?
axis_2_turning_point_timing.why_not_per_bar_agreement: per-bar agreement is dominated by long stable middles. A detector can score well while missing every turn — the 2026-08-08 early-wave analysis measured exactly that shape (first-quintile agreement 30.8% against fifth-quintile 90%). Turning points are events, so they get an EVENT-level metric.

metrics.detection_lag_distribution: bars from each label turning point until the classifier shows the new state — median AND interquartile range, not the median alone
metrics.hit_rate_recall: share of label turning points detected within a horizon of one quarter of the label's own median run
metrics.false_alarm_rate_precision: classifier switches that do not correspond to any label turning point within the same horizon
metrics.event_f1: harmonic mean of the two, the single comparable number
metrics.lag_profile: agreement as a function of applied shift, to catch a PHASE-SHIFT ARTIFACT — on 2026-08-08 an exp-weighted variant posted an eye-catching early-wave number whose lag profile peaked at NEGATIVE lag with only 53.2% agreement, i.e. shifted early into noise rather than leading.

axis_2_turning_point_timing.gate: event F1 must exceed the best VAL-eligible no-learning baseline's event F1, and median detection lag must not be worse than that baseline's.

axis_3_block_structure.question: Does the classifier reproduce the label's block structure, or merely its average?
axis_3_block_structure.why_the_median_is_not_enough: a detector with the correct MEAN run length but the wrong distribution shape — all runs near-identical versus a heavy tail — is not reproducing the structure. Median run alone cannot see this.

metrics.run_length_distribution: two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov (and Anderson-Darling) between the classifier's and the label's run-length distributions, per state
metrics.occupancy_match: per-state occupancy difference, reported per state so a chop-heavy label is not scored as if it were balanced
metrics.switch_count_ratio: classifier switches divided by label turning points; 1.0 is structural parity, >>1 is confetti, <<1 is over-smoothing
metrics.coverage: always reported ALONGSIDE agreement, never folded into it — a candidate reaching high agreement by abstaining on the hard half is a known trap in this project (70.5% at 33.9% coverage on 2026-08-08)

axis_3_block_structure.gate: run-length KS statistic must be SMALLER than the best VAL-eligible no-learning baseline's, and the switch-count ratio must lie in [0.5, 2.0].

decision_rule.hierarchy: Axis 1 is a GATE; axes 2 and 3 are the COMPARISON among candidates that clear it. Validity first, then fidelity. A classifier that reproduces a label whose states are statistically indistinguishable has reproduced nothing.
order: 1a on the label — if it fails, the LABEL is rejected and no classifier is trained
1b on each candidate — a candidate that destroys the label's separation is rejected regardless of axes 2-3
axes 2 and 3 rank the survivors; both must beat the no-learning baseline
decision_rule.adopt: 1a passed AND 1b passed AND axis-2 gate AND axis-3 gate, on a single OOS read

cross_cutting_requirements_inherited_fro: a NO-LEARNING definitional baseline (the causal-zigzag family) is mandatory on every axis; every learned candidate in this project that failed to beat one turned out to be worthless
a Stage-0 regression gate inside the script: rebuild the frozen incumbent on identical rows/splits and HALT unless it reproduces
state the label's theta / scale with every number; a single-scale scorecard is not evidence
floors are derived from the LABEL being evaluated, never carried over from another contract

EVALUATE A GATE IN THE SAME STAGE THAT SELECTS THE KNOB THAT GATE MEASURES — violated twice on 2026-08-08 (transformer, then G3), where a persistence floor was applied at an inherited lambda and rejected families before the persistence knob was ever tuned
early-stop deep models on an INNER split carved from TRAIN, never the project VAL window
exactly ONE OOS read per contract
explicitly_reported_but_never_selected_o: traded return, for continuity with the earlier contracts and so the agreement-vs-PnL divergence stays visible — clearly marked as NOT a gate
the candidate that would have won with no run floor, so the floor's cost is visible rather than hidden
known_hard_bar: Axis 1 is not a formality. The one property already tested this way (variance ratio on czz4) FAILED with a 67x VAL/OOS reversal, and the regime differential died train->OOS on all three assets. A label passing axis 1 would be the first in this project to do so.

artifacts.first_instantiation: to be named by the run that adopts it
